definitions.explanation: A state of well-being and contentment.

examples.japanese: {幸|しあわ}せな{人生|じんせい}
{家族|かぞく}と{一緒|いっしょ}にいるときが{一番|いちばん}{幸|しあわ}せだ。
examples.english: I'm happiest when I'm with my family.

examples.japanese: あなたに{出会|であ}えて{幸|しあわ}せです。
examples.english: I'm fortunate to have met you.

examples.japanese: こんなに{素晴|すば}らしい{仕事|しごと}に{就|つ}けて、{本当|ほんとう}に{幸|しあわ}せなことだ。
examples.english: It's truly fortunate to have gotten such a wonderful job.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{地震|じしん}があったが、{家族|かぞく}が{全員|ぜんいん}{無事|ぶじ}だったのは{幸|しあわ}せだった。
examples.english: There was a big earthquake, but it was a blessing that the whole family was safe.

notes:
{幸|しあわ}せ functions as both a noun (happiness) and a na-adjective (happy). A fundamental word for expressing well-being and contentment.

FORMS:
- Na-adjective: {幸|しあわ}せな{人|ひと} (a happy person)
- Adverbial: {幸|しあわ}せに{暮|く}らす (to live happily)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{幸|しあわ}せに: Best wishes! (said at weddings)
- {幸|しあわ}せ{者|もの}: lucky person
- {幸|しあわ}せを{感|かん}じる: to feel happiness
- {幸|しあわ}せになる: to become happy

KANJI VARIANTS:
- {幸|しあわ}せ (standard)
- {仕合|しあわ}せ (archaic/literary)

RELATED:
{幸|さいわ}い is a related word meaning "fortunately" (adverb) or "good fortune" (noun), but uses a different reading.
